### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/objectql`, touching **51** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/objectql/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**28** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json cbf6956fe49db78c5bdd2b76e2502dff7427aa4b`.

⛔ **11** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/objectql/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `ObjectQL (symbol, 80 pages)`
- **4** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **27** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json cbf6956fe49db78c5bdd2b76e2502dff7427aa4b` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `5d62072168a372e4b873c14fa15382d5d5c3abfc` — the merge of head `c0730d4173b748df025a11ec5157abbde2a7de08` into base `cbf6956fe49db78c5bdd2b76e2502dff7427aa4b`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 5d62072168a372e4b873c14fa15382d5d5c3abfc && git checkout 5d62072168a372e4b873c14fa15382d5d5c3abfc
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin cbf6956fe49db78c5bdd2b76e2502dff7427aa4b c0730d4173b748df025a11ec5157abbde2a7de08 && git checkout -B drift-repro cbf6956fe49db78c5bdd2b76e2502dff7427aa4b && git merge --no-ff c0730d4173b748df025a11ec5157abbde2a7de08

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json cbf6956fe49db78c5bdd2b76e2502dff7427aa4b
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs cbf6956fe49db78c5bdd2b76e2502dff7427aa4b` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `dd8df6b3f977d7adbd5088ced985caa8c4f9eeaf`
Local-runs: none

The code is identical to `825dc866`: `dd8df6b3` changes only the changeset's `Clause-②:` line. The review was run by an independent reviewer and is adopted by the seat.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Which doors fill.** All three named doors fill, and only after the storage sync:
  - live `saveMetaItem` captures in publish mode, after `put()` and before the write-through (`protocol-save.ts` ~2128), and fills after `ensureObjectStorage`, the audit and the emit (~2185);
  - `publishMetaItem` captures before `runPublishSideEffects` and fills after the announce;
  - `publishPackageDrafts` captures before `registerAdmittedBatchRows` and fills after its side-effect loop, reporting per promoted draft.
- **What counts as changed.** The change signature is `{type, expression, scale}` with sorted keys. It catches a new field, formula→stored, plain→stored, and a changed expression, type or scale. An unchanged field is never walked, and a draft save captures and fills nothing. Pins: a draft leaves `[null, null, null]`, an unchanged field records no updates, and the card's case runs formula→stored, then `[1,2,3]`, then a total of 6, in the unit test and through the real `POST /analytics/dataset/query` (dogfood).
- **Failure handling.**
  - A refused storage sync means no fill and a per-field `stored-expression-fill-incomplete` warning.
  - A thrown fill is caught, logged and reported.
  - A failed or skipped row, an unreadable object or a truncated walk each produce a per-field warning that names what is left and the remedy.
  - The door answer stays `success`, and the definition stays live.
- **Boot and CLI.** Boot still only announces (`announceStoredExpressionHoles`). Hydration and peer apply take no capture. `os migrate stored-expressions` is untouched.
- **Count reporting.** The per-field count rides the existing `advisories` key on all three answers, and the tests parse each answer through its response schema.

### ② Semver level

- **What widens.** The published faces are all in `@objectstack/objectql`: `ObjectQL#captureStoredExpressions`, the exported type `StoredExpressionCapture`, and the `fields` option of `backfillStoredExpressions`. The new advisory rule ids add no field, because `rule` is free text in `packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts`; precedent `object-storage-sync-refused`, #30635.
- **Declaration.** `Clause-②: yes (widening)` + `Metadata-protocol: none` + `patch`. The changeset was corrected at `dd8df6b3`; the seat corrected the PR body.
- Nothing previously accepted is now refused.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Only engine-computed values are written: the patch holds the stored computed fields plus the row's own stored `updated_at`. The caller supplies only the definition, never row ids or values.
- The system context is the same constant the CLI uses (`isSystem` + `preserveAudit`), applied by the same `backfillStoredExpressions`. `preserveAudit` only lets the supplied `updated_at` stand: hooks, roll-ups and audit writers still see an ordinary write. Every door is gated by `manage_metadata`. No relaxation beyond the CLI path.
- Tenancy: definitions are environment-wide (`refuseOrganizationScopedWrite`, write-through at `organizationId: null`), so an unscoped walk inside this engine's datasource matches the definition's scope.
- Should-fix S2: on a live server, a row is written back with the `updated_at` from its page read. A user write landing in that window has its `updated_at` rolled back. The values stay correct, because the update recomputes from the fresh row. The CLI's occupancy gate guards this; the door does not. A fix round is owed.
- Should-fix S1: `rollbackMetaItem` and `revertCommit` make a changed definition live with no fill. The ruling names save and publish only. The seat files a follow-up card, and the fill module's docblock is to name the two as not filling.
- Accepted, not changed: the fill is one synchronous walk inside the request (measured ~0.7 ms/row, 100k rows ≈ 68 s), as the #24253 publish backfill is. This is the confidence gap the ruling left to the dev to measure; it was measured, and is reported to the maintainer.
- Nits: the dogfood draft negative checks only that the notice is absent; the PR body's Acceptance notes still say `Clause-②` "declared `no`"; `duplicatePackage` / `importUnmanagedPackage` fill but drop the per-field report; the batch fill runs before `applyPublishBackfill`, so the count describes the pre-backfill state; `field` + `fields` together let `fields` win silently; per-row `logger.warn` volume is the same as the CLI.

**VERDICT: PASS**

domain:server#1 · os-sales · session_01L6bhgVaKJ9TPfXPRhdqx3e

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `5c740006c812171b6010e9b216427407414348d3`
Local-runs: none

Delta review of `dd8df6b3..5c740006` (patch round 2, six files, +168/-17), on the declaration face (`Clause-②: yes (widening)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, amendment 6820941403). The earlier record 6821120243 at `dd8df6b3` covers the rest of the PR and is not re-judged. Run by an isolated reviewer and adopted by the seat. Check-runs on this head: 58 runs, 39 `success`, 19 `skipped`, none failing or pending (Lint & Repo Gates, TypeScript Type Check, Test Core 1/8 to 8/8 and Dogfood Regression Gate all `success`).

### ① Derived judgments

- **S2 guard, the conditional write.** `writeUnlessMovedSince` (`stored-expression-backfill.ts`) sends each fill write through `engine.update` with the module-internal `WRITE_PRECONDITION_OPTION` set to `{ updated_at: stamp }`. The engine lowers that to `driver.updateMany` over `{ id, updated_at }` plus a readback (`updateByIdExpecting`, ADR-0142 D4), and zero rows matched raises `CONCURRENT_UPDATE`. The fill catches that code inside the retried closure, so it is an answer and is never retried. It then reads the row again: another stamp, or no row, answers `moved` and nothing is written; the same stamp is written unconditionally. This closes S2 of the earlier record: a write that lands between the page read and the fill write keeps its own `updated_at`.
- **Why a moved row needs no fill.** Read in `engine-update.ts` and `applyStoredExpressionsToPatch`: every engine update, by id or by predicate, computes all stored computed fields over the merged row and writes each one that differs from the prior row. The doors start the walk after the definition is live and the storage is synced, so an engine write of this process that moves a row mid-walk stores the value itself. The claim holds for that case; its limit is should-fix F1 below.
- **Fallback paths.**
  - No stamp (the object declares no `updated_at`, or the row's is blank): written unconditionally, as before the round. Nothing can regress.
  - Federated object: `hasUpdatedAt` is false through `isFederatedUnprovisionedInjectedColumn`, so the stamp is `undefined`, the patch names no `updated_at` and no predicate is issued on it. The new ledger row matches the code.
  - Driver with no `updateMany`: the engine writes unconditionally and warns once per process. This is the behaviour before the round, so no regression.
  - Stamp spelling the driver's own predicate does not equal: detected by the re-read with `sameStoredValue`, then written unconditionally. Safe, and it degrades to the earlier behaviour.
- **CLI.** `os migrate stored-expressions --apply` calls the same `backfillStoredExpressions`, so it gets the guard with no change in `packages/cli`. Its `--json` answer prints the report whole and so gains the `concurrentRows` keys; the text report gains one line when the count is above zero. The exit code logic is untouched: a moved row is not a gap.
- **Counts and notice text.** `concurrentRows` is bumped after the retry settles, on the report and on each field of the patch; `written` is not bumped for a moved row. The door notice takes `concurrentRows` off `left`, so a moved row does not turn `stored-expression-filled` into `stored-expression-fill-incomplete`. The sentence is appended to both notices only when the count is above zero, so an answer with no concurrent write reads as at `dd8df6b3`.
- **Pin and ablation.** The new test moves the second row (new `end_day`, stamp `2099-01-01T00:00:00.000Z`) after the first keyset page is read. It asserts the stamp stays, the value is the edit's own (10), the column reads `[1, 10, 3]`, and the notice says `2 rows of 3 written` and `1 row written by another write while the fill ran`. The fixture's `updateMany` evaluates the `where` it is given, so the pin passes through the real precondition. The release note records the ablation turning it red; it was not re-run here.
- **Ledger row.** `stored-expression-backfill.ts#writeUnlessMovedSince :: updated_at` with disposition `writer`, an existing disposition. Accurate.
- **`cli.mdx` row.** The three routes named match the doors the PR fills, and the rollback and revert sentence matches the S1 docblock. Accurate.
- **Dogfood.** The draft-time total now asserts 400 `DATASET_INVALID` (both `status` and `code`), which closes nit N1 of the earlier record.

### ② Semver level

- **Inside the declaration.** No new export from either package entry (`index.ts` and `core.ts` are untouched in the delta). `WRITE_PRECONDITION_OPTION` and `CONCURRENT_UPDATE_CODE` stay module-internal. No new error code, no change to `ERROR_CODE_LEDGER` or `StandardErrorCode`, no change under `packages/spec`. No new field on a door answer: the count rides the message text of the existing advisories, and the rule ids are unchanged.
- **One widening the amendment and changeset do not name.** The exported types `StoredExpressionBackfillReport` and `StoredExpressionBackfillFieldOutcome` gain a required `concurrentRows: number`. It is additive on a value the package produces, it stays within `yes (widening)` and `patch`, and nothing accepted before is refused. See should-fix F2.
- `StoredExpressionFillReport` in `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` is not exported from the entry; its `concurrentRows` is optional.

### ③ Boundary flags

- The precondition is carried by a module-private symbol, so no door and no caller option can set it. The write context is unchanged (`isSystem` + `preserveAudit`); the re-read uses the system context and reads one row by id. No new input from the caller reaches the write.
- **F1, should-fix.** `moved` trusts that the write which moved the row computed the field under the live definition. That holds for an engine write in the process whose definition is live. It does not hold for a peer node that has not yet applied the change, or for a write that did not go through the engine: such a row is left as it was, counted as computed, and the notice can still say nothing is left to do. Before this round the fill wrote that row. The window is narrow and `os migrate stored-expressions --changed --apply` repairs it. Follow-up: on `moved`, compare the re-read row with a recompute, and write it under the new stamp or count it as left.
- **F2, should-fix (prose face).** The changeset and the PR body should name `concurrentRows` on the two exported report types and on the `--json` report, and say that the command's writes are now conditional. The seat checks this at ACCEPT.
- **Nits (none blocks).**
  - `1 row ... were not written over`: number agreement in the notice sentence.
  - A row deleted mid-walk is counted as `written by another write`.
  - The same-stamp fallback is silent, so on a driver whose predicate never equals its own read the guard is off with no signal.
  - The engine's one-time warning for a driver with no `updateMany` speaks only of claims and the round-robin cursor.
  - Two comments are now behind: `concurrent-update-error.ts` says `Two users today`, and `WRITE_PRECONDITION_OPTION` names only the assignment cursor.
  - `beforeUpdate` hooks run on a write the precondition then refuses, and twice on the same-stamp fallback, as they do for the claim gate.
  - The `cli.mdx` row does not mention the guard.
- PR author is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`.
